chunks: He narrated - Al-Husayn ibn Sa'id from Muhammad ibn Abi Umayr from Sa'id ibn Ghazwan from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) who said:
I asked him, 'How much should be given to one man from the zakat?' He said, 'Give him from the zakat until you make him self-sufficient.'
ai.seo_question: How much zakat should be given to a single poor person to make them self-sufficient?
ai.summary: In *Tahdhib al-Ahkam*, Shaykh al-Tusi records this narration from Imam al-Sadi’ (AS) to clarify that the minimum zakat distribution is determined by functional self-sufficiency (*ghina*) rather than a fixed monetary threshold. This principle ensures that the recipient is elevated above the state of dependency, aligning with the Shia juristic emphasis on the transformative purpose of charity rather than mere subsistence. It reflects the broader Islamic objective of empowering individuals to become independent contributors to the community.
